description: Session 10 golden set for retrieval evaluation. Project descriptions and cross-collection questions, each hand-annotated with the documents that are genuinely relevant. Q1–Q5 are budget-only (graded over data/budgets_sample.json) and keep the original relevant_budget_ids; Q6–Q8 span the multi-index corpus (budgets + transcripts + technical docs) and use relevant_source_ids. A retrieved chunk counts as relevant iff its source_id (budget_id / transcript_id / doc_id) is in the relevant set. The distractors are deliberately cross-sector or cross-collection 'similar but irrelevant' documents — the exact failure modes this session attacks (averaged multi-topic queries, the dominant collection flooding the top-k, lexical identifiers diluted by embeddings). Annotation criterion: a document is relevant when it directly addresses the asked-for functionality/topic, not merely shares sector or vocabulary. NOTE (2026-07-02, Session 11 pre-work): Q1-Q7's relevant_*_ids were corrupted during the S10-live multi-collection port (commit f53df4c) — they were copy-pasted from the official repo's BUD-2024-001..017 numbering scheme, which does not exist in this repo's data/budgets_sample.json (whose 15 budgets use a different, non-sequential id scheme seeded in Session 7). Every Q1-Q5 relevant id was silently unmatchable, so any precision/recall computed against this file since f53df4c was meaningless. Re-annotated against the real corpus by re-reading data/budgets_sample.json + data/transcripts_sample.json + data/technical_docs_sample.json; ids below are verified to exist. Q8 was already correct (references no budget id).

queries.query: Mobile banking application with OAuth2 authentication, PSD2 open banking compliance, strong customer authentication and a transaction ledger.
queries.note: Fintech auth + payments. Bullseye BUD-2024-014 (mobile banking API, OAuth 2.0, instant payments). BUD-2024-040 (card issuing with a double-entry ledger) is the transaction-ledger relative. Trap: BUD-2024-070 (fashion app with mobile wallets) is e-commerce payments-like but not banking; BUD-2024-090 (digital lending) is fintech but lending, not banking auth.

queries.query: Headless e-commerce storefront with a product catalog, shopping cart checkout and personalized product recommendations.
queries.note: E-commerce storefront/catalog/checkout/recommendations. Bullseye BUD-2024-021 (headless storefront, real-time search, one-page checkout). BUD-2024-070 (fashion app with recommendations + mobile wallets) and BUD-2023-015 (grocery store catalog/checkout) are storefront relatives. Trap: BUD-2024-099 (marketplace re-platforming to microservices) is e-commerce but infra work, not a storefront; BUD-2024-040 (card issuing) is a cross-sector payments lexical trap.

queries.query: Telemedicine platform for patient appointment scheduling and video consultations with HL7/FHIR integration and clinical records.
queries.note: Healthcare telemedicine/scheduling. Bullseye BUD-2024-052 (telemedicine, video consultations, e-prescription). BUD-2023-008 (EHR with appointment scheduling + FHIR interoperability) and BUD-2023-045 (multi-clinic scheduling + lab integration) are scheduling/clinical relatives. Trap: BUD-2024-081 (remote patient monitoring, wearables) shares the healthcare sector but is monitoring, not scheduling/telemedicine.

queries.query: Industrial IoT platform ingesting sensor telemetry for predictive maintenance and real-time equipment monitoring in a factory.
queries.note: Industrial telemetry/monitoring. Bullseye BUD-2024-033 (industrial IoT, SCADA telemetry, predictive maintenance). BUD-2024-061 (smart factory quality control, PLC connectivity, machine vision) is the factory-monitoring relative. Trap: BUD-2023-034 (robotic cell control, digital twin) is industrial but robotics control, not telemetry-driven maintenance.

queries.query: Real-time payments gateway with fraud detection, transaction reconciliation and a double-entry ledger.
queries.note: Fintech payments/ledger. Bullseye BUD-2024-040 (card issuing platform with double-entry ledger, KYC, webhooks). BUD-2024-014 (mobile banking, instant payments) is the payments relative. Trap: BUD-2023-015 (grocery store checkout) and BUD-2024-070 (mobile wallets) are e-commerce lexical near-misses; BUD-2023-027 (retail investing app) is fintech but investing, not payments.

queries.query: What did the client say about the Stripe Connect checkout, and how much did marketplace vendor payouts cost?
queries.note: Cross-collection: TR-2024-002 (ShopFlow headless commerce meeting) explicitly discusses a Stripe Connect checkout for marketplace vendor payouts; BUD-2024-021 is that same project's budget (headless storefront, one-page checkout with Stripe); DOC-PAYMENTS-API's 'Stripe Connect onboarding' section covers vendor payouts verbatim. Routing should hit transcript + budget + technical_doc. Trap: a single budgets index would miss the transcript discussion entirely.

queries.query: How do we integrate predictive maintenance with SAP using IDoc/BAPI, and what was discussed about it?
queries.note: Lexical identifiers (SAP, IDoc, BAPI) the embeddings dilute — hybrid search should lift the exact-match doc/transcript. TR-2022-004 is the FactoryOps industrial IoT meeting; BUD-2024-033 is that project's budget (SCADA telemetry, predictive maintenance engine); DOC-SAP-INTEGRATION specifies IDoc/BAPI work-order creation from predictive-maintenance alerts. Routing should span technical_doc + transcript + budget.

queries.query: Reference for OAuth 2.0 authorization-code flow with PKCE and PSD2 strong customer authentication.
queries.note: Documentation-shaped query: should route to technical_doc (and the auth meeting). Trap: budget components mention auth but do not answer a 'how-to/reference' question.
